name: DCB Bank Ltd
title: DCB Bank Ltd - 532772 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: Clean Q2 FY27 print (ROA 1.03%, ROE 14.6%) but NIM fell on FCNR liquidity carry; management guided NIM up in Q3–Q4 and held ROE guidance from prior call, with new capital still unclosed.

summary.headline: DCB Bank Q2 FY27 net profit rose 29% YoY to INR 236 crore, a record, with ROA 1.03% and ROE 14.6%, while NIM slipped on surplus liquidity.
summary.overview: Advances grew 21% YoY and deposits 19%, with net interest income up 17% and revenue up 21%. Cost to income fell to 59.64%, an 18-quarter low, and cost to average assets was 2.47%. Asset quality improved: GNPA 2.29%, NNPA 0.73% (both 23-quarter lows), PCR 81.38%, and credit cost 0.28%. NIM declined QoQ because the bank carried surplus liquidity from a $194 million FCNR(B) raise, which management expects to reverse from Q3 as repo-linked loans reprice.

financial_highlights.change: +29% YoY; highest ever quarterly, fifth consecutive record

financial_highlights.value: 19% YoY (18.6% per management on Q2 basis)

financial_highlights.change: Core fee income described as strong
+7.23 pp YoY; ex technical write-off 68.75%, +9.6 pp

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: About 23% of total assets, with ~INR 14,000 crore book and NPA of INR 26 crore; management is comfortable taking share to 25% but not beyond. Roughly 30% organic and 70% inorganic (co-lending and DA).

segments.name: Mortgages / LAP
segments.commentary: Incremental mix about 70:30 home loan to LAP (71:29 per management). Balance transfers from NBFCs are a target segment, priced without rate cuts; mortgage growth was described as muted so far and expected to pick up.

segments.name: Corporate / NBFC lending
segments.commentary: Corporate is about 8% of the asset book, mostly NBFC exposure via co-lending and DA; management sees it rising toward 10%. Management says the book delivers good ROE with low historical NPAs.

segments.name: Agri and PSL
segments.commentary: Tractor book about 4%, KCC about 4%, individual MFI about 1% of the book; management says these are behaving well with low bounce rates. No state exceeds 20% of asset exposure.

segments.name: Bancassurance / cross-sell
segments.commentary: Management expects a bancassurance commission drop under draft norms and sees cross-sell as slow to ramp, with results possibly over 12 to 18 months. Analysts estimated a 10-12 bps ROA hit.

guidance_outlook: NIM expected to improve in Q3 and Q4 FY27 even without further rate hikes, as surplus liquidity runs off and repo-linked asset repricing begins in November.
Opex trend and cost to average assets expected to continue at similar levels; headcount expected around 12,800-12,900 by year-end, not 13,000.
About 20 new branches in the year, mostly in existing locations.
Credit cost to remain well below the 0.28%-plus guidance level; growth guided at 18-20%.
FY27 ROE guidance of 13.5% expected to be exceeded; capital raise could change the ROE guidance, and management declined to issue a new FY28 target.
Gold loan share capped at 25% of assets.
ECL model with a Big 4 advisor expected to be up and running by March; SMA-1 and SMA-2 reduction is the next credit-cost lever.
capex_capacity: Employee count at 12,002, up sequentially by about 450; growth is directed to existing branches for both assets and liabilities.
Branch network up about 3 in the quarter; about 20 branches planned for the year.
Floating provisions of about INR 218 crore held, with a stated 5.93x cover of operating profit by provisions.

Capital raise: management said it is near closure on three components, with a firm commitment expected within weeks to about a month, before the next investor call; the bank has not raised equity since 2017. Management said it will not raise below book value.
demand_pricing: NIM fell QoQ as surplus liquidity from the $194 million FCNR(B) window (August) was carried for most of the quarter; the NIM is around 3.3% against a guided 3.5-3.6% range, per an analyst.
Deposit cost reduction attributed to a conscious non-highest-rate strategy and repricing of long-tenure term deposits; top-20 deposit cost is under 7%.
Management says LAP demand is strong with a stable rejection rate; about one-third of LAP borrowers are arbitrage cases, a third seek better products and the rest need more exposure.
Gold prices are fairly stable at around INR 14,560 per gram (999 gold). Management names gold price decline as the main risk.
Management cites a bancassurance fee drop as the main earnings headwind, and said other levers will be needed to offset it.

qa_highlights.question: Is opex growth elevated, and will headcount reach 13,000 with 20 branches added this year?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex growth was driven by people costs and normal cyber-security tech spend, with no one-offs. Headcount is 12,002 and is expected to reach about 12,800-12,900 by year-end; about 20 branches are planned.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NIM decline QoQ, and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Surplus liquidity from the FCNR(B) raise was carried for most of the quarter; lending yield fell 2 bps QoQ. Management expects NIM to improve in Q3 and Q4 as repo-linked loans reprice in November, and as credit costs stay low.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the gold loan book growing faster than disbursements, and are gold slippages rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth includes inorganic DA and co-lending, while disbursement figures are organic only. Non-gold slippage rose to 1.55% from 1.52%. Management said some co-lending and DA partners collect before NPA, so the 1 DPD rule does not apply to many of them.

qa_highlights.question: Ex-FCNR(B), what was the lending yield and margin, and will the expansion continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give an ex-FCNR NIM figure. It said lending yield fell 2 bps and that yield should rise with repo hikes, with a fairly decent NIM expansion expected next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL readiness and impact on PCR and credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: A Big 4 firm has been appointed; the ECL model is expected to be live by March. Management said lead indicators are positive except SMA-1 and SMA-2, and sees credit-cost gains from SMA reduction after ECL.

qa_highlights.question: Will ROA/ROE guidance be revised, and how will bancassurance fee loss be offset?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to set a new ROE target until capital comes in; it expects ROE above 13.5%. On bancassurance, it cited the prior loss of about INR 100 crore of treasury gains and said it will wait for final norms and build offsets.

qa_highlights.question: Is gold loan CIBIL screening relaxed, and what is the risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Low CIBIL is not a bar for gold loans; management uses it to profile customers. The main risk is a fall in gold prices, and auction recovery was under 10% during the MFI stress, per management.

qa_highlights.question: How are the drought and agri books, and what is the mortgage outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Tractor and KCC books are about 4% each and collections remain robust, with no state above 20% of exposure. Management expects mortgage share to rise as gold is capped at 25% and overall growth is 18-20%.

risks_watch: Non-gold slippage edged up to 1.55%, and SMA-1 and SMA-2 are elevated; ECL transition and the related model risk are to be tested by March.
Gold loan book, co-lending and DA partner collection practices and gold price exposure.
Bancassurance commission drop under draft norms; management has not quantified the offset, and analysts estimated a 10-12 bps ROA hit.
Capital raise: terms and price are not yet disclosed; management said it will not raise below book value.
NIM recovery depends on repo pass-through and on deposit repricing lagging asset repricing.
summary.management_tone: Confident and firm on asset quality, cost and profitability. Management was evasive on NIM ex-FCNR(B), product-wise repricing mix, and the size and price of the capital raise, citing ongoing negotiations.
key_quotes: So we got more than what we deserve in terms of foreclose -- what you call, prepayment penalty, etcetera, and lesser interest rate.
Below the book value, we will not raise capital. That much I can tell you.
So it's about -- it's from that perspective that you'd be looking at the CIBIL.
So, we are stockpiling liquidity post February '26 Israel-Iran war.

adds.what: About 20 new branches planned for the year, mostly in existing locations

growth.why: Management guides growth of 18-20% and ROE above 13.5% for FY27, backed by about 20 branches, roughly 450 headcount added in the quarter and expected NIM recovery from Q3 as surplus liquidity reverses, though no concrete capacity or order numbers were given beyond branch count.
